chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, from his book, said: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father and Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

“With the Qa'im (peace be upon him) there will be a small number of Arabs.” It was said to him: “But those who describe this matter among them are very many.” He said: “People must be tested and distinguished, and sifted, and a great multitude will be thrown out from the sieve.”

key_terms.الْغُرْبَالُ: The sieve, used metaphorically for the process of distinguishing true from false
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (the Awaited Imam), a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.يُغْرَبَلُوا: To be sifted (like grain through a sieve)
key_terms.يُمْحَصُوا: To be tested or purified by removing impurities

ai.seo_question: Who are the true followers of the Qa'im during the occultation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* addresses the theological anxiety of the early Shia regarding the 'disagreement' (ikhtilaf) among followers during the Minor and Major Occultations. It employs the metaphor of sifting (gharbala) to explain that the proliferation of claimants and the eventual purification of the community are divine necessities, ensuring that only the truly steadfast remain with the Qa'im.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (6) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ahmad bin Yousuf al-Ju’fi Abul Hasan from Issma’eel bin Mihran from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abu Hamza from his father and Wuhayb bin Hafs from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“There will be a very few Arabs with al-Qa’im (as).” It is said to him: “But those, who talk about this matter among the Arabs, are so much many.” He said: “People must be tried, sifted and purified. Much many people will be thrown away from the sieve.”
